analysis: Documentation-only PR: docs/provider/cli-reference.md (head excerpt, unchanged lines 1408-1621 show provider run marker, APNs push history, LaunchAgent env passthrough, provider.toml keys) and docs/reference/configuration.md. The configuration.md patch (hunks at line 52 and 66) adds `logout` to the drain --timeout setting row and a new section 'Provider endpoint resumption and logout'. It documents: DARKBLOOM_NATIVE_SERVE_QUALIFICATION (exact `1` only, not forwarded to launchd, accepts no caller-provided signing key/hash/hardware/privacy claims, does not enable production coordinator resumption); an endpoint-resumption capability with no new env var/config key (fixed process-key responder, protocol 1 advertised in registration with a fresh per-socket nonce; absent responder omits both fields); and `darkbloom logout --config` accepted for compatibility but not used to retarget revocation (issuer metadata bound to saved token; missing metadata => local-only logout with warning). No code changes are in this batch, so the actual implementation (ProviderLoop+Serve.swift, CoordinatorClientCodec.swift registrationMessage, LogoutCommand.swift, DeviceAuth.swift AuthTokenStore.issuer, NativeServeQualification.swift) and the coordinator-side handling of the resumption nonce/proof are not reviewed here. The documented design is consistent with threat model assumptions (T-053 replay, T-052, TB-011: wire contract does not create local trust or alter proof validity). Cross-file items for later passes: the logout design avoids sending a saved token to an attacker-chosen --config URL (SSRF/credential-forwarding analog of T-017); verify the code matches that doc, and that resumption does not bypass final-dispatch authorization checks. No security regression identifiable from the docs alone; no threat model update demanded by these text changes. Coverage limit: the referenced anchors (protocol-messages.md, cli-reference logout section) are not in the supplied units.
